$comment: FIRST-PARTY AI REFERRAL DATA from Panda Patches, a founder-affiliated store.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Almost no business can break out AI assistants as a
revenue source. Most report near-zero AI traffic, and the reason is
measurement rather than reality: ChatGPT strips referrers, its mobile apps
do not pass them, and a large share of people read an answer and then type
the domain directly. Panda Patches captures referrer WHERE IT SURVIVES and
asks the customer where it does not, which is why these numbers are not zero.
RELATIONSHIP, STATED NOT BURIED. Panda Patches is owned and operated by a
PandaCodeGen co-founder. This is operating experience, not independent client
proof, and any page rendering it must say so.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT: lead-to-order conversion rates. The lead card
and the order card do not share a window, and repeat orders appear to inherit
the original lead source. Computing a rate across them produced Claude at
133% and Facebook at 96%, which is structurally impossible. Rather than
publish a softened version of a broken number, the rate is omitted and this
note explains why. Do not add it back without confirming both cards cover
the same range and that repeat orders are excluded.

source.relationship: Founder-affiliated. Owned and operated by a PandaCodeGen co-founder.
source.system: Custom operations platform built on Next.js, Sanity, Supabase and Square
source.method: Referrer captured where it survives; self-reported source collected at quote request where it does not. Both fields feed one source value.
source.limitation: One business, one vertical (custom embroidered and printed patches), one window. These are not industry benchmarks and no claim is made that they generalise.

orderWindow.label: 1 March to 18 August 2026
orderWindow.note: Both totals exclude Web Checkout (48 orders, $10,295.11), which the platform treats as a fulfilment route rather than an acquisition source and already excludes from its own revenue total. Excluding it from the order count too keeps both figures describing the same population; mixing them was an error caught by summing the rows against the declared totals.

corroboration.instrument: Google Search Console, Performance, Generative AI features (Beta)
corroboration.note: Independent of the platform's own attribution. Two unrelated instruments pointing the same way is the reason this is offered as evidence rather than as a claim.
corroboration.limitation: Impressions in Google's generative surfaces, not clicks and not revenue. It corroborates direction, not the dollar figures.

outlierDisclosure.note: Average order value of $6,120 against a site average of $348.91, almost certainly bulk or wholesale. Removing it moves the AI revenue share from 6.2% to 6.5%, so it works against the headline rather than for it.
